name: Henry Despenser
description: Bishop of Norwich, previously a soldier, who suppressed the East Anglian rising on his own initiative and without a royal commission -- marching from Stamford with a small force of men-at-arms and archers, relieving Peterborough, reclaiming Cambridge and Norwich, and defeating Geoffrey Litster's rebel army at the Battle of North Walsham around 25-26 June 1381. He executed captured rebels, including Litster, without formal trial -- technically outside his legal authority, though never punished for it given the outcome.
narrative_function: The one regional suppression carried out by force before royal commissions could be organized.
